name: Coffee seat
summary: A café table for two in a one-to-one chat: the one who reached out already has a steaming cup, the other cup sits empty; times are chalked on the café's board, the friend taps one and her cup fills and it lands on both calendars, or taps 'Not this week' and a saucer keeps the seat, no guilt.
useWhen: omg we havent talked since august, coffee?
free for kettle and crumb this week? tue 3 wed 10 or thu 4
miss you!! lets get lunch soon
can we grab a coffee before break, my treat
dontUseWhen: a group of three or more picking a time (use meeting-time)
a date or romantic plan (use date-deck)
picking where to go rather than when

title.description: Card title, e.g. 'Coffee at Kettle & Crumb'

host.description: Who reached out (a name in the chat)

guest.description: Who they asked (a name in the chat); only they pick

quote.description: What the host said, in their own words

since.description: How long since they talked, e.g. 'since August'; may be empty

place.description: The café or spot, e.g. 'Kettle & Crumb'

hostOrder.description: The host's usual order, under their cup

guestOrder.description: The guest's usual order, shown when her cup fills

note.description: A short chalk note at the foot of the board, e.g. 'lowkey my treat'; may be empty

picked.description: Index of a time already picked, or -1 for none
